overview: This bill extends, through 2030, the authorization for federal funding to monitor, assess and research fish and fisheries in the Great Lakes Basin. The program, run through the U.S. Geological Survey's Great Lakes science work, was set up in a 2020 spending law and its funding authorization was set to run only through 2025. The bill makes no other changes; it simply swaps the end year from 2025 to 2030. Actual dollar amounts would still have to be provided in yearly spending bills. As of September 15, 2025, the House Natural Resources Committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say steady research funding helps track invasive species, fish populations and water conditions in the Great Lakes, which support fishing, tourism and drinking water for millions of people.
against: Critics say extending the program for five more years without changes skips a chance to review whether it is working well or whether the money could be better used elsewhere.
